note.text: Inclusive OR permits either or both and fails only when both are false. Exclusive OR requires exactly one true alternative. State the intended reading. Denying one alternative of an accepted OR requires the other; affirming one does not exclude the other under inclusive OR.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish inclusive from exclusive or, evaluate each and infer the remaining alternative when one is denied. Builds on: compound propositions and truth-value evaluation in the conditional lesson. Leads to: accurate translation and later truth tables for logical connectives.

sections.heading: Alternatives joined by or
sections.text: A disjunction combines propositions as P or Q. In the default formal convention here, or is inclusive: P, Q or both can make it true. Both false makes it false. For an invented Douala club notice, a message can be printed or sent electronically, allowing both methods. Do not silently read an extra not both into that statement.

sections.heading: Exactly one is a different rule
sections.text: An exclusive disjunction requires one true alternative and one false alternative. A task that says choose drawing or poetry, but not both explicitly uses that rule. Both true then fails, as does both false. Ordinary either…or can depend on context, so these exercises always specify the reading instead of asking pupils to guess the speaker’s intention.

sections.heading: What follows from denying an alternative
sections.text: If P or Q is accepted and P is false, Q must be true: otherwise both would be false. But if P is true, inclusive OR leaves Q open. This difference matters when translating everyday rules. Neither P nor Q denies both; it is not another spelling of P or Q.

mistake.wrong: P OR Q and P prove that Q is false.
mistake.right: Inclusive OR allows P and Q together.
mistake.why: Only an added exclusive condition rules out both.

worked_example.problem: The fictional notice permits printing or electronic delivery, inclusively. Printing was not used. What must hold if the notice was followed?
steps: At least one allowed method must have been used.
Printing is ruled out by the additional premise.
Without electronic delivery both alternatives would be false.

cards.idea: Inclusive OR permits either or both.
example: A printed and electronic notice can satisfy inclusive OR.

cards.idea: Inclusive OR fails only when both claims are false.
example: At least one true claim is enough; both true is allowed.

cards.idea: Exclusive OR needs different truth values.
example: Exactly one means both true is forbidden as well as both false.

pick.q: Accept “Bih reads or Ayuk writes” inclusively, and also accept that “Bih reads” is false. What follows?
w: Ayuk writes is false.
Bih reads is true.
Neither alternative’s truth is constrained.
e: That would make both alternatives false, contrary to the accepted OR.
This contradicts the given denial of that alternative.
Denying one accepted alternative leaves the other required.
